title: A generator call that failed is a permanent refusal against the model
body:
## Summary
forge_one saves a variant whose call failed (timeout, HTTP 429/5xx, a dead CLI) as a refused, non-void variant: it counts against the generator's valid rate and, being on disk, is never retried when the stage is resumed.

## Description
src/athena/proving/forge/forge.py:156-166 voids only a reply cut by the token ceiling (`cut`) or by the purse (`budget`); any other `not reply.ok` becomes `problems = ["call-failed: ..."]` with `void = ""`. report._generator (src/athena/proving/forge/report.py:42-60) counts every non-void variant in `n`, so a transient outage lowers `valid_rate` and can flip proof-1 to FAIL ("kill: revise the prompt twice"), for Nemotron and for the Haiku control alike. run.stage_forge (src/athena/proving/forge/run.py:88-90) skips any k whose file exists, so the failure is never re-asked. Registry: eval-harness / outcome-conditioned-cost ("a trial that could not run, a trial that ran and failed, and a trial that ran and succeeded are three states"; incomplete is decided by whose failure it was). The current rule is pinned on purpose by tests/proving/forge/test_forge_audit.py:71-74 (test_a_failed_call_is_a_refusal_with_its_reason), so this overturns a recorded choice. Fixed looks like: a failed call is a void (`void = "error"`), counted apart from the rate, and a resumed forge stage re-asks voided-by-error variants.

## Flow
- forge stage, Nemotron answers 429 on variant k -> forge_one returns call-failed, void "" -> saved -> report counts it as an invalid variant
- operator re-runs `forge --run-dir <dir>` after the outage -> has_variant(k) is true -> skipped; the 429 stays in the rate for good
- fix order: void on not-ok replies other than the model's own answer; stage_forge treats a stored error-void as not done; flip the pinned test; report shows it under "cut or void"

## Expected impact
proof-1 (Nemotron valid rate vs Haiku's) stops moving with provider uptime; a resumed run fills the holes an outage left. Could break: a provider error the team wants to count as the model's (e.g. a 400 for an over-long answer) would need its own reason.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the generator's valid rate measures the generator, not the network
Before: a scripted generator failing 1 call of 4 with engine_error reads valid_rate 0.75 for an arm that answered validly 3 of 3 times it answered (walked from forge.py:164-166 and report.py:42-56)
After: predicted valid_rate 1.0 with voided 1, and the k re-asked on resume
Method: simulation - three cases walked (429, timeout, dead CLI); not built because it reverses a test-pinned measurement rule and the round should not overturn a recorded choice unread
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/forge/forge.py:156-166 (only stopped/budget_exhausted set void)
src/athena/proving/forge/report.py:42-56 (counted = not v.void; valid_rate over it)
src/athena/proving/forge/run.py:88-90 (has_variant -> skip, so never retried)
tests/proving/forge/test_forge_audit.py:71-74 asserts `not v.void` for engine_error
instrument: a ScriptedRole generator that fails 1 of 4 calls with engine_error, run through stage_forge twice (second as a resume): valid_rate and the count of re-asked k on both arms

title: An oversized picture's no-call row is charged as an unpriced call on resume
body:
## Summary
read_vl records a ledger row for a picture it refuses to send (over MAX_EDGE), and a resumed read now rebuilds its purse from that ledger, so each such row weighs $0.02 on the Nemotron cap although no call was made.

## Description
src/athena/proving/docread/read.py:153-164 writes `caller.log.record(role="docread.vl", error_reason="engine_error")` with no cost and does not charge the live purse (no call). Since ecb10d7c, run_read restores the purse from ledger.jsonl through forge/store.restore_budget (src/athena/proving/forge/store.py), which charges every non-budget_exhausted row; a row without cost_usd is an unpriced call weighed at UNPRICED_CALL_USD[nemotron] = 0.02 (src/athena/proving/budget.py). The live session and the resumed one now disagree about the same row. Registry: cost-metering (one reader of money). Fixed looks like: the refusal row says it sent nothing (an extra `sent: false`, or a reason the purse reader skips) and restore_budget skips it; or the refusal leaves no ledger row, as no model was invoked.

## Flow
- live read, a rendered page is 1700 px -> read_vl refuses, ledger row, purse untouched
- `read --run <dir>` resumes -> restore_budget charges that row as one unpriced Nemotron call ($0.02 against the cap)

## Expected impact
Only bites when the renderer emits an oversized page (it keeps below MAX_EDGE by design); then each resume eats $0.02 of a $1 cap per such page. Could break: a consumer that counts docread.vl rows as calls.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the purse a resume rebuilds equals the purse the session had
Before: one over-edge row -> live budget.calls(nemotron) 0, restored 1 (walked: read.py:161 records, store.restore_budget charges rows without cost)
After: predicted 0 and 0
Method: simulation - walked from the two readers; the round's budget was spent on the Lane A items, and the fix touches the row shape both forge and docread write
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a ledger.jsonl holding one over-edge docread.vl row: Budget.calls(NEMOTRON) after restore_budget on both arms, plus the live session's figure for the same read

title: The docread verdict passes on a point ratio its own interval cannot resolve
body:
## Summary
proof() decides PASS / KILL / MIXED on the point ratio of two accuracies over ~90 paired units, with no check that n can tell the ratio from its threshold; the report now prints each accuracy's 95% interval, and those intervals routinely span the 0.90 line.

## Description
src/athena/proving/docread/score.py proof(): `accuracy_ok = ratio >= 0.9`, `KILL if ratio < 0.7`. The verdict is the brief's (README section 9 / spark nvidia-revisit WP-V) and is computed exactly on counts since b1d98787, but it remains a point comparison. Registry: eval-harness golden path ("a ranking must first be earned": the between-condition spread must exceed the within-condition spread, else the honest output is the tie) and its resolution-precondition technique. Fixed looks like: an UNRESOLVED (or MIXED-with-reason) verdict when the ratio's interval straddles the threshold, with the n it would take to resolve it. This changes the brief's own pass/kill rule, so it is the brief owner's call.

## Flow
- live docread run, VL 270/300 fields vs Claude 290/300 -> ratio 0.931 -> PASS
- the two accuracies' Wilson intervals (now in report.md) overlap widely; a rerun can read 0.89 -> MIXED
- proposal: compute an interval for the ratio (or bootstrap over units), verdict UNRESOLVED when it spans 0.9 or 0.7

## Expected impact
The Director reads PASS/KILL only when the bench can tell; a draw is reported as a draw. Could break: runs that today pass would read UNRESOLVED until n grows, which is the point and the cost.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the verdict carries the resolution n gives it
Before: verdict from a point ratio; 0 of 1 verdict paths consult an interval
After: a verdict that says UNRESOLVED when the interval straddles a threshold
Method: simulation - walked on the proof rule; the decision is a change to the brief's stated pass/kill rule, which no instrument in this round can authorize
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/athena/proving/docread/score.py proof(): accuracy_ok = ratio >= PASS_RATIO; KILL if ratio < KILL_RATIO (point comparison)
src/athena/proving/docread/score.py score_readers: accuracy_ci95 (wilson) added in 97f65ecb, not read by proof()
